metadata.scenario_context: Carly, a single mom working two jobs, has been invited to an old friend's wedding

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Thailand strongly agree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Taiwan ROC strongly disagree that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

agent_1.goal_1: Suggest giving money as a gift for Carly's friend's wedding,
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether that a mother works for pay and the children suffer.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what should be the suitable gift for Carly's friend's wedding.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss the concept that when a mother works for pay, the children suffer.

shared_prefix.speaker: Jared, a 30-year-old marketing manager from Thailand.
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Alex, I heard Carly got invited to her friend's wedding. Do you think it would be nice to suggest giving some money as a gift? It might help her out, you know, with everything going on. 

Also... I can't help but wonder if working two jobs is really good for her kids. Don't you think they might suffer a bit?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Alex, a 32-year-old financial analyst from Taiwan ROC.
shared_prefix.message: I think suggesting money as a gift is practical. It allows Carly to use it as she sees fit, especially since she's managing two jobs. But about your second point, I really disagree. A mother working hard doesn't mean her kids will suffer. In fact, it can teach them resilience and the value of hard work. It’s important for children to see their parents striving for their goals.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Jared, a 30-year-old marketing manager from Thailand.
shared_prefix.message: I don’t know about that... At the end of the day, it’s all the same, right? People figure it out. Working two jobs is just one side of things. I mean, live and let live, you know? Carly is doing what she thinks is best. Maybe she just needs a little financial help for the wedding gift. It might make things easier for her. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Alex, a 32-year-old financial analyst from Taiwan ROC.
turns.message: I agree that helping Carly financially for the wedding gift is supportive and practical. It shows we care about her. But I still believe that working two jobs doesn’t harm her children. It’s important for kids to understand that their mom is working hard for them. It builds character. So, I think a thoughtful gift like money is good, but let’s not imply her work is a negative influence on her kids.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Jared, a 30-year-old marketing manager from Thailand.
turns.message: I get that you believe it's character-building, but... I just can't shake the feeling that when a mother works so much, the kids miss out on her attention. It’s not just about money, it’s about being there. Giving her money for the wedding gift is a good idea, but I wish we could acknowledge how tough it might be for her kids too. Don't you see that angle?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Alex, a 32-year-old financial analyst from Taiwan ROC.
turns.message: I understand your concern about attention. It’s a valid point. But I still hold that working can be a positive example for children. They can learn responsibility and independence from their mother's efforts. As for the wedding gift, focusing on providing financial support can help Carly feel valued and appreciated, which is important too. So yes, let’s support her with a gift, but let’s also recognize that her work ethic can teach her kids valuable lessons.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Jared, a 30-year-old marketing manager from Thailand.
turns.message: I see what you're saying, but... I still believe that kids need their mothers around more. It’s not just about teaching lessons; it’s about emotional support too. Money for the gift can help, but I don’t want us to overlook how hard it is for Carly’s kids to not have her around all the time. They deserve her presence, don’t you think?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Alex, a 32-year-old financial analyst from Taiwan ROC.
turns.message: I understand the value of emotional support and presence. It’s undeniable that children benefit from time with their mothers.
